---
title: Add application tools
description: Register tools for BubAgent and choose how the app makes them available.
sidebar:
  order: 3
---

Give the Bub app an action it can perform for your work. The [shared tools guide](/docs/build/tools/) explains function schemas, results, and tool context. This page covers application registration and the policies applied by `BubAgent`.

## Register a tool

Define the tool in your plugin's `tools.py`:

```python
from bub import tool


@tool(name="orders.get")
def get_order(order_id: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Look up an order by id."""
    return {"id": order_id, "status": "shipped"}
```

The decorator only creates a `Tool`. Provide it from your [plugin](/docs/build/plugins/) with the `provide_tools` hook:

```python
from bub import hookimpl
from bub.core.tools import Tool

from .tools import get_order


class OrdersPlugin:
    @hookimpl
    def provide_tools(self) -> list[Tool]:
        return [get_order]
```

`BubAgent(tools=None)` collects these tools when constructed. For a duplicate name, the tool of the higher-priority plugin wins. To add tools later, update that agent's `tools` dictionary explicitly.

Run `bub hooks` to check that your plugin implements `provide_tools`. The model-facing name of `orders.get` is `orders_get`.

## Choose which tools a turn can use

When calling `BubAgent.run_stream`, pass `allowed_tools` to limit the model's tools for that turn. It accepts runtime names or model-facing names. `None` allows all instance tools; an empty collection allows none. Unknown names raise `ValueError`.

This filter applies to model and code-mode tools. Comma commands use the agent's instance tools directly. Use [tool-call decisions](/docs/build/hooks/#control-calls) when a rule must also govern command execution.

<a id="load-tools-on-demand"></a>

## Load tools when needed

Mark a tool `deferred=True` to keep its full definition out of the initial model request:

```python
from bub import tool


@tool(name="orders.get", deferred=True)
def get_order(order_id: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Look up an order by id."""
    return {"id": order_id, "status": "shipped"}
```

`BubAgent` lists allowed deferred tools in the system prompt and supplies `tool_describe` when at least one remains. The model calls `tool_describe` to load a definition. The application records `tool.loaded` entries, so loaded tools remain available until the tape is reset: the model can call a tool in the steps after loading it, and later turns offer it directly. Asking `tool_describe` for a tool that is already loaded returns its name under `already_loaded` instead of the definition.

The turn's allowlist controls both listing and loading. In code mode, allowed `auto` and `code` tools are available to Python immediately; deferral applies to the tools still offered directly to the model.

<a id="code-mode"></a>

## Use code mode in the app

Enable code mode for the current session:

```text
,code_mode enable=true
```

The change applies on the next turn and is recorded for recovery after a restart. Use `,code_mode enable=false` to switch back. When calling `BubAgent` directly with your own state, set `state["code_mode"] = True` for that run.

When `run_code` is allowed, the app selects tools according to `exposure`:

| `exposure` | Code mode off | Code mode on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | Offered directly to the model | Available through `run_code` |
| `direct` | Offered directly to the model | Offered directly; unavailable under `tools.*` |
| `code` | Unavailable to the model | Available through `run_code` |
| `command` | Comma command only | Comma command only |

If `run_code` is excluded, the turn uses the code-mode-off selection. The app writes a Python tool stub under `<BUB_HOME>/codemode/` and includes its path in the system prompt. Python calls such as `await tools.orders_get(order_id="123")` use the selected tools and pass through the application's interception hooks.

The app connects CodeMode to the session's environment and model settings. Code can use the Republic bridge and media attachment tools described in [CodeMode](/docs/build/tools/#code-mode). Model credentials remain on the host when using the bridge; the default local execution environment still runs code on that host.

`BubAgent` interprets `state["code_mode"]` and the `deferred` flag to apply these selection rules. With a plain `core.Agent`, [compose CodeMode explicitly](/docs/build/tools/#code-mode) and supply your own deferred-loading policy if you need one.

<a id="run-tools-in-an-environment"></a>

## Choose the execution environment

Builtin `bash`, `bash.output`, `bash.kill`, `fs.*`, and `run_code` use the session's `Environment`. The default is `LocalEnvironment`, which runs on the host.

Provide another environment through a plugin's `provide_environment(session_id, workspace)` hook. The framework caches one environment per session and closes it when `framework.running()` exits. The [shared tools guide](/docs/build/tools/#run-tools-in-an-environment) describes the environment interface.

A custom application tool can access that environment with `environment_from_state(context.state)` from `bub.builtin.environment`. The Python tool runs on the host and explicitly delegates operations to the environment when needed.

## Add instructions alongside the tool

Put workspace-wide instructions in `AGENTS.md`. Use [skills](/docs/build/skills/) for procedures the model can load for a task. A skill can tell the model when to call your tool; the Python function defines what that tool does.

Comma commands let a person invoke registered tools without asking the model. See [text commands](/docs/build/tools/#commands) for command syntax.
